data.name: Sree
data.gender_notes: Sree is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Sree is a name of Lakshmi, the Hindu goddess of wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. She is the consort of Vishnu and is often depicted with gold coins and lotus flowers. The name Sree carries the meaning “Goddess of Wealth and Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sree usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of wealth and prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes abundance, prosperity, and good fortune.
data.etymology: Sree belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of Wealth and Prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sree total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Sree" holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism. It is often used at the beginning of Sanskrit phrases and auspicious words to invoke the blessings of Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth. It is also used as a prefix for the names of deities, temples, and sacred texts. The name is also a sign of respect and reverence, often found at the beginning of letters or documents.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lakshmi is believed to be the embodiment of material and spiritual wealth. The name "Sree" serves as a reminder of the abundance and prosperity that the divine mother can bestow upon us. It also serves as a reminder of the importance of material wealth in one's spiritual journey. The use of the name "Sree" in religious rituals and practices is believed to bring about prosperity and good fortune in both worldly and spiritual matters.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sree is a revered prefix in Hinduism, symbolizing auspiciousness, prosperity, and divine blessings. It is believed to bring good fortune and ward off negative energies.
